result.title: TMT: Adapting CLIP to Infrared Imagery via Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer
result.summary: Vision-language models such as CLIP achieve strong performance across computer vision tasks, yet their image-text alignment is less reliable for infrared (IR) imagery because large-scale pre-training is dominated by visible-spectrum data. Due to the high cost of the infrared-text labeling, we investigate adapting CLIP to IR through only paired infrared-visible images, which requires considering modality-specific knowledge while preserving scene content and CLIP's image-text alignment. To achieve this, we propose TMT (Text-Derived Modality Knowledge Transfer), which adapts CLIP's image encoder through a text-defined infrared-to-visible direction and supervision from paired IR-visible images. First, we found that modality discrepancy can be described by corresponding text embeddings, thus using the direction of text embedding differences to guide the knowledge transfer between visible and infrared modalities without erasing infrared-specific information. To enhance the representation of semantics and details of infrared images, we introduce Generative-Perceptual Co-Supervision that combines semantic alignment from CLIP visible image encoder with diffusion noise-prediction feedbacks. On four source-disjoint IR classification benchmarks, TMT achieves the highest mean zero-shot accuracy among the compared methods (48.92%). It also achieves the best IR-text retrieval results among the compared methods without infrared-text supervision during adaptation and the highest open-vocabulary segmentation mIoU on both CART and SemanticRT among the CLIP-like methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TMT，在缺少红外-文本标注的情况下仅用配对红外-可见图像适配 CLIP 图像编码器：用文本嵌入差值方向刻画红外到可见的模态迁移方向，并结合 CLIP 语义对齐与扩散噪声预测反馈进行生成-感知协同监督。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「扩散噪声预测作为细节感知监督」与「文本嵌入差值定义模态方向」可能为 LVR 中保持视觉细节、抑制 latent 状态漂移的训练监督提供可核查线索，但原文不做推理期状态生成、证据获取或停止决策，迁移需自行设计。
